primary_hypothesis.natural_language_mechanism:
Best-supported working hypothesis is an ICT-type emissive state whose nonradiative decay is reduced upon aggregation primarily by rigidification. Target-side aTB indicates strong, distributed electronic redistribution (E35, E36) with limited net structural relaxation (E37) and high shape/rigidity proxy (E39). The only observation anchor available is aggregate-state emission at 630 nm (E70) with aggr-only coverage (E72) and medium observation reliability (E73), consistent with an AIE-like “restricted relaxation” picture but not uniquely diagnostic of TICT vs ICT.
Unresolved boundary is mainly ICT vs TICT. The self torsion trend is reported as “mid” with a decrease direction (E31), but the absolute torsional change is far below the “no torsion” cutoff (reasoning_config.thresholds.atb_dihedral_thresh_none=8.0), so torsion-enabled access to a twisted minimum is not strongly supported by target-only aTB. Comparative context complicates this: the target’s abs torsion change is unusually high vs the local neighbor distribution (E21) and, when label-stratified, is closer to the ICT-labeled neighbor group on that axis (E23), while the electronic gap-change axis is not strongly separating (E22, E23). ESIPT is weakly supported structurally (compact prior shows no proton-transfer prerequisites; E57), so it is kept as a low-probability alternative rather than a co-lead.
